skill.name: translate
skill.description: Translates Markdown and plain text between languages with glossary, locale, style, and formatting guidance. It defaults to Chinese and supports long-file workflows.
skill.summary: Translate Markdown and plain text with consistent terms, tone, and locale choices.
skill.author: FuHehe12

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown backtick notation, binary-search variables, and UTF-8 Chinese sample prose. I confirmed three medium-risk workflow instructions that run Bash commands for splitting, merging, and cleanup; the bundled Python scripts do not spawn subprocesses.

remediation.issue: Bash examples use placeholder paths for splitter and merge commands.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer structured command execution with argv arrays, or document strict path quoting and validation before running the scripts.

remediation.issue: Cleanup instructions include recursive deletion with rm -rf.
remediation.suggestion: Replace recursive shell cleanup with a scoped deletion routine that verifies the generated _parts directory before removal.

content.value_statement: Long translations often lose tone, terms, and Markdown structure. This skill builds a glossary, translation brief, and workflow for consistent document translation.
actual_capabilities: Translates Markdown and plain text between any language pair, with Chinese as the default target.
Creates a temporary glossary and translation brief before translation starts.
Splits long Markdown files into segments with context for parallel translation.
Guides sub-agents to preserve tone, terminology, Markdown, links, and code blocks.
Merges translated segments and checks headings, code block closure, and link formatting.
Supports locale-specific language choices through reference guidance.
limitations: PDF, Word, web pages, and images must be converted to Markdown first.
Large-file workflows use local Python scripts through Bash.
Glossary writeback needs user confirmation before persistent files are updated.
The skill guides translation quality, but it does not certify legal or medical wording.

use_cases.title: Localize Developer Documentation
use_cases.description: Translate Markdown docs while preserving code blocks, links, headings, and technical terms.

use_cases.title: Translate Research Notes
use_cases.description: Render academic or technical notes into another language with consistent terminology and formal tone.

use_cases.title: Adapt Product Copy
use_cases.description: Translate product pages or README text for a target locale without losing concise marketing style.

prompt_templates.title: Translate a Short File
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate `docs/intro.md` into zh-CN. Preserve Markdown, links, code blocks, and frontmatter. Create the glossary and translation brief first.

prompt_templates.title: Translate to a Locale
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate translation with regional wording requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate `guide.md` into Japanese for readers in Japan. Keep technical terms consistent and explain any uncertain term choices.

prompt_templates.title: Translate Multiple Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate all Markdown files in `docs/` into zh-CN. Share one glossary and one translation brief. Use parallel segment translation after confirming the plan.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Translation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refinement of an existing translated file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refine `manual_zh.md` against the glossary and translation brief. Improve naturalness, terminology consistency, and Markdown formatting without adding new content.

output_examples.input: Translate a 400-line README from English to zh-CN.
output_examples.output: Produces a zh-CN Markdown file, plus a brief glossary and translation brief that document key terminology and tone choices.

output: Reports a split-and-merge plan before processing.
Creates segment files with local context for each translator.

output_examples.input: Translate product copy for Taiwan readers.
output_examples.output: Uses locale-specific vocabulary and records the target locale in the translation brief.

best_practices: Provide the target locale and audience when wording needs regional precision.
Review the generated glossary before approving large batch translations.
Keep source files under version control before running split and cleanup workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to translate PDFs, images, or Word files without converting them first.
Do not skip the glossary and translation brief for speed.
Do not run cleanup commands from an unknown working directory.

faq.question: What file types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Markdown and plain text. Other formats should be converted to Markdown first.

faq.question: What is the default target language?
faq.answer: The default target language is Chinese, with zh-CN as the default locale.

faq.question: Can it translate large documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can split long Markdown files, translate segments in parallel, and merge them after checks.

faq.question: Does it preserve Markdown formatting?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs agents to preserve headings, lists, tables, links, frontmatter, and code blocks.

faq.question: Can it use my preferred terminology?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads a user glossary and creates a document glossary before translation starts.

faq.question: Does it update the source file?
faq.answer: No. The workflow writes translated output to a separate file with a language suffix.
